meta.pageTitle: GATE CSE Digital Logic Previous Year Questions – Solved PYQs

questions.text:
Let, [latex]x_{1} \oplus x_{2} \oplus
x_{3} \oplus x_{4}=0[/latex] where [latex]x_{1},  x_{2} ,
x_{3} , x_{4}[/latex]  are Boolean variables, and  [latex]\oplus[/latex] is the XOR operator.
Which one of the following must always be TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]x_1\oplus x_2\oplus x_3\oplus x_4=0\Rightarrow x_1\oplus x_3=x_2\oplus x_4[/latex].

Complementing both inputs of an XOR does not change it ([latex]\bar a\oplus\bar b=a\oplus b[/latex]), so [latex]\bar x_1\oplus\bar x_3=\bar x_2\oplus\bar x_4[/latex] is always true.

The other options fail for x = 1111 (XOR = 0, but the product is 1, and so on).

Answer: Option 3

questions.text: Consider an eight-bit ripple-carry Combinational Circuit for computing the sum of A and B, where A and B are integers represented in 2's complement form. If the decimal value of  A is one, the decimal value of B that leads to the longest latency for the sum to stabilize is ________.
questions.solution:
The longest delay happens when a carry is generated at bit 0 and has to ripple through all 8 bits. A = 0000 0001, so B should be all 1s: 1111 1111 = [latex]-[/latex]1.

Answer: -1

questions.text:
Consider the two cascaded 2-to-1 multiplexers as shown in the figure.

The minimal sum of products form of the output X is
questions.solution:
First mux (select P): output = R if P = 1, else 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] PR.
Second mux (select Q): X = PR if Q = 1, else [latex]\bar R[/latex].

[latex]X=\bar Q\bar R+QPR[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\bar Q\bar R+PQR[/latex]

questions.text: We want to design a synchronous counter that counts these quence 0-1-0-2-0-3 and then repeats. The minimum number of J-K flip flop srequired to implement this counteris ________.
questions.solution:
The sequence 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 3 has 6 steps, and the three 0s are followed by different numbers, so the counter needs 6 different internal states.

6 states need [latex]\lceil\log_2 6\rceil=3[/latex] flip-flops (the output is then decoded from the state).

Answer: 3

questions.text: The 16 bit 2's complement representation of an integer is 1111 1111 1111 0101;   its decimal representation is__________ .
questions.solution:
The MSB is 1, so the number is negative. Take the 2's complement of 1111 1111 1111 0101:
invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1010, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1011 = 11.

Answer: -11
